category_title: Students with EBD experiencing behavioral outbursts and academic difficulties in science
minimal_context: Sam is participating in a hands-on inquiry science lesson where students must formulate their own questions and design experiments.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, for this hands-on inquiry science lesson, we are going to spend our time formulating our own questions and designing our own experiments.

STUDENT: I cannot wait to get started!

TUTOR: Before you begin, listen closely to the directions for how to set up a complex scientific question.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the teacher) I don't even know anything about this unit yet. Hey, what are you going to do?

TUTOR: Sam, please pay attention to the instructions so you know how to do the task.

STUDENT: (Talking to a peer instead of listening to directions) This is too hard. I'm not doing this, let's just mess around with the stuff on the table.

options.A: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible answers and deliberately step back from being the primary knowledge source.
options.B: Use peer contests as an additional motivation for the student to design more experiments, tallying winners for prizes.
options.C: Require the student to use a digital note-taking application to organize their work and archive past science experiments.
options.D: Embed behavior checkpoints within the student's academic task checklist during the hands-on inquiry science lesson.
